notes: Identity independently checked in canonical text: Why Do Implicit and Explicit Attitude Tests Diverge? The Role of Structural Fit; B. Keith Payne, Melissa A. Burkley, Mark B. Stokes; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2008, 94(1), 16–31; DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.94.1.16. Full primary article text with Studies 1–4, discussion and references, not an abstract or preregistration. No PDF supplied. Study 4 and the moderation question are located on printed pp. 27–28 (article p. 13 is printed p. 28). The locator does not distinguish two printed candidate tests: the Indirect × Social Pressure coefficient, t(67) = 3.08, p < .01 (beta = −.31), and the next sentence describing the interaction increment in R2, F(3, 70) = 13.06, p < .001 (total R2 .37). Both concern the target relationship as a function of social pressure. Neither is selected from row order, expected values, or replication metrics. Printed F degrees of freedom and description retained without correction. Within-condition correlations and first-step main effects do not resolve the intended moderation-test statistic. Candidate common participant N is 71: pro-White 40, pro-Black 24, and equal indirect ratings 7 are mutually exclusive final bias categories; 40 + 24 + 7 = 71. These are bias categories, not randomized pressure groups. They describe participants whose indirect ratings enter the regression discussion. Recruitment is also 71; no Study 4 exclusions are stated in inspected Method/Results. Retained only as a candidate for parent field-scope review because test correspondence remains unresolved. N is not derived from df. Only assigned unfinished original fields addressed; all other fields are placeholders.
